walkthroughs.body_html:
Consequences Of Uses Of Computing — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Consequences Of Uses Of Computing brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Consequences Of Uses Of Computing.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which UK Act makes unauthorised access illegal?
options: Data Protection Act
Computer Misuse Act 1990
Copyright Act
Freedom of Information Act
Software patents
Personal data
Network bandwidth
Open source code

mcqs.q: What is the main advantage of asymmetric encryption?
options: Secure key exchange without sharing a secret in advance.
Copy code from any unrelated class.
It is faster than symmetric encryption.
It is impossible to break.

mcqs.q: What does an INNER JOIN return?
options: Only rows with matching values in both tables.
Only the inner columns of each table.
All rows from both tables combined.
It is impossible to break.

mcqs.q: What does inheritance allow a subclass to do?
options: It is impossible to break.
Replace the superclass entirely.
Copy code from any unrelated class.
Reuse and extend the attributes and methods of its superclass.
